annotations.title: Beth Numbers as Iterated Power Sets
annotations.body: The beth hierarchy is defined recursively: ℶ₀ = ℵ₀, ℶ_{n+1} = 2^ℶₙ. Equivalently, ℶₙ = |𝒫^n(ℕ)| — the n-th iterated power set of ℕ. Since |ℝ| = ℶ₁ = 2^ℵ₀, we have |𝒫ⁿ(ℝ)| = ℶ_{n+1}. In Lean 4, Cardinal.beth_succ captures the recursion: beth (Order.succ o) = 2^(beth o).

annotations.title: The Three-Step Proof Chain
annotations.body:
|𝒫(𝒫(ℝ))| = 2^|𝒫(ℝ)|   [Cardinal.mk_set]
= 2^ℶ₂               [parent: card_powerSet_real_eq_beth_two]
= ℶ₃                 [beth recursion: Cardinal.beth_succ]
Each rewrite is a single Mathlib lemma, making the proof a three-line composition.

annotations.title: Converting ℕ Indices to Ordinals for Cardinal.beth
annotations.body: Cardinal.beth takes an Ordinal argument, but n+1 is a natural number. The key lemma beth_nat_succ converts (n+1 : ℕ) cast to Ordinal to Order.succ (n : Ordinal) via: rw [Order.succ_eq_add_one]; push_cast; ring. This pattern appears throughout the file.

annotations.title: iteratedPowerSet as a Lean Recursive Definition
annotations.body: The type iteratedPowerSet : ℕ → Type is defined by well-founded recursion: iteratedPowerSet 0 = ℝ, iteratedPowerSet (n+1) = Set (iteratedPowerSet n). This gives a concrete Lean type for each level of the power set hierarchy, enabling the universal quantification in card_iteratedPowerSet_eq_beth.

annotations.title: Cantor's Theorem Drives Strict Monotonicity
annotations.body: At each level n, Cantor's theorem gives #(iteratedPowerSet n) < 2^#(iteratedPowerSet n) = #(iteratedPowerSet (n+1)). This is exactly Cardinal.cantor applied to the current cardinality. The strict tower inequality follows by induction, with transitivity handling arbitrary m < n.

annotations.title: Beth Equalities vs. Aleph-Index Independence
annotations.body: The beth equalities |𝒫ⁿ(ℝ)| = ℶ_{n+1} are unconditional ZFC theorems — no CH or GCH required. In contrast, the aleph-index questions (is ℶ₂ = ℵ₂? is ℶ₃ = ℵ₃?) are independent of ZFC by Easton's theorem. The beth hierarchy provides a canonical labeling of these cardinalities that is stable across all models of ZFC.
